verbalization: Carmustine, a heteroorganic entity classified as an antineoplastic alkylating agent, is linked to Temozolomide through a shared biological property of alkylating activity. This mechanism is central to the treatment of malignant glioma, as Temozolomide is known to induce DNA damage in cancer cells, leading to cell death. The integration of Carmustine into this pathway suggests a potential role in glioma treatment, though the direct therapeutic effect of Carmustine remains less well characterized compared to Temozolomide. The evidence highlights a dependency on alkylating agents, which may be a key mechanism in the context of glioma therapy, though further research is needed to clarify its clinical relevance.
